verdict.rationale: React's own docs state that on the server React can start streaming HTML while data is still being fetched, progressively filling in content before any JavaScript loads. This matches the story's goal of faster perceived loads before client code arrives. Supporting docs cover server rendering via Node and hydrateRoot attaching React to server-rendered HTML. Missing for 10: API-reference detail for the streaming APIs themselves (e.g. a streaming render function or Suspense boundaries), and independent or hands-on corroboration of perceived-load gains.

support.subject: As a developer, I can stream server-rendered content so pages get faster perceived loads before all client code arrives

citations.quote: On the server, React lets you start streaming HTML while you’re still fetching data, progressively filling in the remaining content before any JavaScript code loads.
React can also render on the server using Node
Call `hydrateRoot` to “attach” React to existing HTML that was already rendered by React in a server environment.
